propositions: A committed lock file freezes transitive dependencies, causing any future security advisory on a pinned version to block CI and fail all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes caused or can fix the advisory.

The current pip-audit gating blocks both Gerrit verify and main release CI unconditionally; it should block releases always but block Gerrit verify only when the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, or requirements/constraints files).

When an upstream cap (e.g. inspect-ai capping click) holds the project on a vulnerable version, override-dependencies is the correct remediation tool; uv lock --upgrade-package is a no-op against a cap and constraint-dependencies can only narrow existing constraints, returning UNSATISFIABLE as expected output rather than proof an upgrade is impossible.

The retry logic in the pip-audit job only retries database-unreachable failures, not real findings, yet users universally try recheck first; the gating message and runbook must explicitly state that recheck cannot clear a real advisory.

A periodic scheduled run (following the terraform-drift.yml and prompt-eval.yml pattern) must escalate outstanding transitive-dependency advisories on main via ticket filing with dedup, separate from the Gerrit lane, so main blocks releases on known-vulnerable pins without punishing unrelated authors.
